key_insight: VesNet uses a neural-network surrogate to accelerate expensive vesicle self-interactions in Stokes flow while preserving physically based solvers for the remaining dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical simulation of large deformable-particle suspensions on modest hardware, which is valuable for microfluidics, soft matter, and biomedical flow modeling.
method: Approximates vesicle self-interactions, including background-flow coupling and short-range lubrication forces.
Keeps conventional modules for boundary reparameterization and far-field hydrodynamics.
Runs on GPU for end-to-end speedup over boundary-integral baselines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 100x speedup versus a multithreaded MATLAB CPU solver and about 5x versus a GPU counterpart, while still matching key behaviors in single-vesicle, pair, and large-suspension tests.
watch_item: Because the network replaces only selected interaction terms, accuracy may depend on the training regime and on staying within the flow and geometry conditions represented in the training data.
paper_title: VesNet: Neural network accelerated solver for simulating Stokesian vesicle suspensions
